chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'When we enter Mecca and Medina, do we complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said, 'If you shorten it, that is acceptable; and if you complete it, that is better, you will increase (in reward).'
ai.seo_question: Should travelers shorten or complete their prayers when visiting Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of both shortening and completing prayers in Mecca and Medina is affirmed, with a specific preference for completion. This ruling highlights the unique status of these holy cities as places where the traveler's journey effectively concludes, allowing for full worship. The emphasis on 'greater reward' underscores the spiritual merit of maximizing devotion in the sanctuaries of Islam.
